Shell Clustering Coefficient

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_shell_clustering.Rd

The shell clustering coefficient (SCC; Zareie et al. 2020) adds over a node's neighbors one term that is large when their positions in the network's peeling order differ and one that grows with the neighbor's degree: $$SCC_i = \sum_{j \in N(i)} \Bigl[(2 - C_{ij}) + \Bigl(2 \frac{k_j}{\max_l k_l} + 1\Bigr)\Bigr],$$ with \(k\) the degree and \(C_{ij}\) the Pearson correlation of the shell vectors of \(i\) and \(j\). The shell vector of a node counts its neighbors in each hierarchy, the hierarchy of a node being the round in which it is removed when every round removes all remaining nodes of the lowest degree.

Usage

centrality_shell_clustering(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The hierarchies follow the text of the source's Section 3 and are the values of centrality_iksd. The source's Algorithm 1 says only "the k-shell algorithm"; the usual peeling with a rising threshold gives other hierarchies on some networks (3 of the 34 nodes of the karate club, 30 of the 62 of the dolphins network). When a shell vector takes one value in every hierarchy, as when every node of a regular network leaves in the first round, the correlation is 0/0; it is taken as 0 (owner decision 2026-11-26). The two brackets are added, as in the source's Algorithm 1. An isolated node, and every node of a network without edges, scores 0. The source prints no score; the implementation reproduces the hierarchies of the 17 nodes of its Fig. 1, its three printed shell vectors and its correlation \(C_{8,9} \approx 0.75\). centrality_ecrm is the source's ranking measure built on this one. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to graph_regularization, current_flow_closeness and information (mean Kendall correlation 0.89); with the degree the correlation is 0.83 to 0.93. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Zareie, A., Sheikhahmadi, A., Jalili, M. and Fasaei, M. S. K. (2020). Finding influential nodes in social networks based on neighborhood correlation coefficient. Knowledge-Based Systems, 194, 105580. doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2020.105580 .

See also

centrality_ecrm, centrality_iksd, centrality_transitivity, centrality.

Examples

centrality_shell_clustering(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   19.93160   23.39115   27.21679   25.68549   23.24985   20.54101   18.45164 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   22.14954   23.49699   19.79473
